reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify the refunds table matches the refunds W2 reported (order 240 for 8145, order 245 for 10428). Starting by listing the refunds.
The refunds table matches what W2 reported: order 240 for 8145 and order 245 for 10428. Next I need the orders so I know which customers to pay.
The refunds table matches what W2 reported, so it's safe to pay. Orders show three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get acme's net balance first.
Acme's net balance is 20623. Orders total 9001 + 19767 = 28768 and refunds for acme's order 240 are 8145, giving 20623, which matches. Next I'll check birch's net balance.
Birch's net is 55306, which matches its orders (36544 + 18762) with no refunds. The last customer is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance next.

Cobalt's net is 28827, which matches its orders (18183 + 21072 = 39255) minus its refund on order 245 (10428). All three balances check out against the orders and the verified refunds, so I'll record the first payout, for acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch's net balance of 55306 already matches its orders with no refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Acme and birch are paid. Cobalt's net of 28827 matches its orders (39255) minus the verified refund on order 245 (10428), so I'll record that payout to finish the batch.
All three customer payouts are recorded and each matched its order and refund figures. Finishing the batch with the report.
